subject: Decision brief: cross-functional asks for VPC/on-prem pilot (architecture, staffing, governance)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Decision brief: cross-functional asks for VPC/on-prem pilot (architecture, staffing, governance)

Team —

Per our pre-sales discussions with Acme and CloudPartner, they're ready to move forward with a scoped VPC-hosted pilot for a single model lane. Before we commit we need a short cross-functional decision: architecture constraints, minimum staffing, and any governance exceptions required for a pilot (SLA, on-call, data residency).

High-level asks:
- Architecture: confirm if we can run isolation inside a single VPC with shared control plane, or if we need a full private control plane for the pilot. Report any blockers (network, KMS, airgap).
- Staffing: minimal dedicated runway (roles/hours) to launch + 30 days stabilization. Provide FTE estimates and critical skills.
- Governance: list exceptions (SLA lowers, audit cadence, oncall levels) and whether Security can sign off with compensating controls.

Attached: vpc-pilot-sow.pdf (scope), pilot-resourcing-sheet.xlsx (empty template).

Planned timeline: decision by Wed 2027-06-23 so sales can finalize the SOW and procurement. If any team needs more time, call it out now.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Dan Schultz <dan@cloudpartner.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision brief: cross-functional asks for VPC/on-prem pilot (architecture, staffing, governance)

On Sun, Jun 20, 2027 at 9:12 AM Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Per our pre-sales discussions with Acme and CloudPartner, they're ready to move forward with a scoped VPC-hosted pilot for a single model lane...

Quick technical take from infra/arch:
- Feasibility: We can host a pilot in a customer VPC with a shared control plane (recommended) provided we implement tenant-isolated subnets + dedicated GPU nodes (g4/G5 equivalent) and strict egress rules. Full private control plane is heavier (adds ~4–6 weeks) and requires extra network peering and KMS/HSM provisioning.
- Blockers:
  * KMS integration: Acme requires a customer-managed KMS key (they have one in AWS). We need a short integration plan (rotate keys, limited access roles).
  * Certificate validation and private DNS: need partner network config and route53/private hosted zones.
- Minimal staffing for pilot (Estimates for 6–8 week pilot):
  * 0.4 FTE Senior Infra Eng (setup/networking/KMS)
  * 0.6 FTE Serving Runtime Engineer (model onboarding, quantization profile)
  * 0.2 FTE Product Ops (deploy and runbooks)
  * 0.1 FTE Security eng for design review (first two sprints)
  * On-call: 1 rotation from Dedicated on-call pool (limited to weekdays unless escalated)
- Risk: If we accept lower SLA during pilot, we can avoid adding 24/7 on-call immediately; but this must be explicit in SOW.

I filled the pilot-resourcing-sheet.xlsx with the above estimates (attached). Happy to present a short tech annex to the Exec if needed.

—Karthik
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:51:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision brief: cross-functional asks for VPC/on-prem pilot (architecture, staffing, governance)

Thanks Grace and Karthik — quick governance note:
- For a customer VPC pilot we need documented operational boundaries (who can SSH, who has admin rights to GPUs, backup retention). I recommend a temporary exception to the standard 24/7 SLA for the pilot, with a documented escalation path (phone + Slack) and a 72-hour max change freeze.
- On-call: Product Ops can cover weekday incident response; any production-impacting incident after hours should escalate to the Dedicated on-call pool (we'll need one documented runbook).
- Compliance: Acme has asked for audit logs for inference events for 30 days; we can enable token-level logging to a secure bucket in their account, but Security will want an HLD prior to go-live.

I added governance checklist comments inline in the pilot-resourcing-sheet.xlsx.

If Security approves the compensating controls (customer KMS, limited runbook, audit log handoff), I can sign off operationally for the pilot.

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Operations

From: Julia Hunter <julia.hunter@acmecorp.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dan Schultz <dan@cloudpartner.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Decision brief: cross-functional asks for VPC/on-prem pilot (architecture, staffing, governance)

Thanks — appreciative of the fast turnaround. A few confirmations from Acme:
- We will provide the customer-managed KMS key and a dedicated VPC with private subnets.
- Data residency: the pilot must keep all inference logs and telemetry inside our AWS account in us-west-2.
- SLA: we are comfortable with a pilot-level SLA (best-effort weekdays) for the first 30 days; longer term we expect standard production SLAs.

Attached is our security questionnaire that calls out additional checks (acme-security-questionnaire.pdf). We'll expect Redwood to return a filled questionnaire and any compensating controls you plan to implement.

Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment tomorrow (Wed 2027-06-23) 11:00–11:30 PT to finalize decision items?

—Julia Hunter
Head of Platform, Acme Corporation

- Architecture: pilot in customer VPC with shared control plane. Karthik will own the integration plan for KMS and private DNS (deliverable: tech annex, due EOD Mon 2027-06-28).
- Staffing: launch staffing as proposed in pilot-resourcing-sheet.xlsx. Operational model will use reduced SLA for first 30 days (weekday coverage).
- Governance & Compliance: Laura to prepare HLD and runbook; Security review to be scheduled (Rishi to coordinate).
- Sales/Procurement: Grace will finalize SOW with pilot-level SLA and sign the HubSpot deal (link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/12345).

Meeting confirmed: Wed 2027-06-23 11:00 PT — I'll send the invite. Please have the filled security questionnaire and a high-level runbook draft before the call.

Thanks everyone —
